source_identity.citation: Rulisek, Sebek, Havlas, Hrabal, Capek and Svatos, J. Org. Chem. 2005, 70(16), 6295-6302.
source_identity.title: An Experimental and Theoretical Study of Stereoselectivity of Furan-Maleic Anhydride and Furan-Maleimide Diels-Alder Reactions
source_identity.primary_content_audit: Read the complete publicly indexed author proof, then visually inspect the reproduced original journal tables, experimental procedure, model and fitting caveats. Publisher and primary-author abstract corroborate the 300 K forward rates. Retained artifacts are browser captures of publicly reproduced primary-paper content, not an archived publisher or author PDF.
retention_limitations: Direct author-PDF download returned HTTP 403; indexed primary content was readable, but PDF bytes are not retained or hashed.
The institutional publisher copy and supporting information are explicitly audience-restricted; no restricted content was requested.
Public HTML retrieval returned HTTP 503; only the named visual source captures below are retained. Do not claim a retained full original source.
The reproduction host is not the publisher. Original table and primary-abstract consistency is checked, but an archival original source remains preferable.

locations: Tables 1-3, units, point estimates, interval estimates and confidence footnotes
Section 2, Chemicals; H NMR Measurements and Estimation of Kinetic Constants
Ideal-volume initial-concentration assumption; Bayesian fitting; reaction steps 1-6; concentration rate equations 7-9 and corresponding IV-VI definitions
Kinetics: exclusion of direct endo-exo conversion from the fitted model
Different initial reactant concentrations; kinetic measurements repeated twice; joint confidence limits
Figures 3-4; NMR calibration and mass-balance caveat for longer 300 K measurements

audited_observation_sets.system: Furan (source species 1) + maleimide (3), reversible formation of endo adduct 6 and exo adduct 7
audited_observation_sets.observable: Eight published point estimates and joint-fit interval widths for reversible concentration-law kinetic coefficients

source_conditions.initial_concentration_method: Known reactant volumes with ideal mixing and no volume contraction/expansion assumed; actual numerical volumes and initial concentrations are not tabulated.
source_conditions.concentration_coverage: Experiments repeated twice with differing initial concentrations; plotted concentration trajectories are not transcribed as exact initial conditions.
source_conditions.concentration_regime_caveat: Figures show finite reactant concentrations; dilution and concentration-independent activities must not be assumed from the word solution.

rate_convention.status: Parameters inferred from concentration trajectories under the authors' reversible kinetic model; not independently verified microscopic elementary mechanism or activity-based intrinsic rate constants.

fit_uncertainty.table_representation: Point estimate plus/minus interval estimate, retained as an interval half-width in that coefficient's units.
fit_uncertainty.fitting_method: Bayesian kinetic-model fit; isomer concentration responses included in the objective function.

source_only_ancillary_observations.system: Furan + maleic anhydride, Table 1 at 300 K; not an additional panel case
source_only_ancillary_observations.source_unit_conflict: The conclusion paragraph prints bimolecular units for the Table 1 endo reverse coefficient. The audited model equations and Table 1 explicitly identify it as first-order s^-1; retain the discrepancy rather than silently following the narrative units.

allowed_rate_only_use: Compare a separately produced coefficient at the same temperature, exact declared isotopic solvent, molecularity, channel/stereoisomer and concentration-law convention.
Numerical initial concentrations are not required to quote or compare a fitted coefficient. They are required to reconstruct a concentration-time, lifetime or time-dependent branching experiment.
Report point error and source joint-fit interval information descriptively; do not infer total uncertainty, calibration or independent normal rate distributions.
readiness_blockers: Freeze a separate rate-only scoring protocol, identity/conditions and any scientifically justified acceptance thresholds before inspecting STORCA predictions; this source observation record is not that protocol.
Assess exact CD3CN applicability explicitly. Ordinary CH3CN continuum parameters are not silently equivalent to the experimental isotope solvent.

Match the reversible concentration-law fit and assess concentration/activity dependence, model identifiability and the unreported pressure; the fitted coefficient is not automatically an elementary intrinsic rate.

For lifetime, trajectories or product-distribution scoring, obtain actual initial concentrations, reactant volumes and observation timings or a preregistered uncertainty-aware digitization protocol; do not invent them.
Retain unquantified systematic uncertainty and the authors' NMR calibration/mass-balance caveat, especially longer 300 K experiments.
No joint covariance or complete systematic uncertainty is supplied; the reported half-widths do not define independent uncertain rates for network propagation.
Direct endo-exo interconversion was excluded by the authors using experimental lag and theoretical arguments; this is a model assumption, not a general proof of pathway absence.
Archive an openly accessible original primary PDF when available; retained public-reproduction captures are not an original publisher/author file.

amendment_policy: Preserve this source observation record and captures. Any corrected transcription requires a new dated record with predecessor hash; never adjust this reference or its readiness to obtain agreement with predictions.
